title: How Much of Remote Work Is Actually Run by AI Now?
body_md:
![anthropic.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/how-much-of-remote-work-is-actually-run-by-ai-now/1.png)
*Screenshot of anthropic.com ([source](https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-economic-index-january-2026-report))*

**My view (an opinion, not a measured result): AI is heavily used for documentation-style tasks such as notes, summaries, first drafts and status updates, and I'd expect people to keep ownership of most judgment calls.** The studies cited below measure Claude.ai and Claude API usage, not all remote work, so they cannot give a total share of remote work that AI runs. Any claim like "AI runs half of remote work" needs a definition of "runs" and a measured sample.

## What's Actually Going On

![anthropic.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/how-much-of-remote-work-is-actually-run-by-ai-now/2.png)
*Screenshot of anthropic.com ([source](https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-march-2026-report))*

### Anthropic's usage data keeps flipping on augmentation versus automation

Anthropic publishes an ongoing Economic Index based on usage of Claude. It covers Claude.ai and Anthropic's first-party API, not all remote work, and Anthropic notes that Claude is used for work that is not broadly representative of the US economy.

The ratio has bounced around. The January 2026 report found augmentation at 52% of Claude.ai conversations against 45% automation — a reversal of the August sample, when automation led 49% to 47% — while over a longer window Anthropic still sees a slow rise in automation's share, since augmentation led 55% to 41% in January of the prior year ([January 2026 report](https://www.anthropic.com/research/anthropic-economic-index-january-2026-report)). Then it moved again: the March 2026 report found augmentation increased slightly in both Claude.ai and API traffic ([March 2026 report](https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-march-2026-report)).

Translation: the split has been close and has moved in both directions, so these data don't show a steady march toward automation. They describe how Claude is used, not whether jobs are being replaced.

### The API side is a different animal entirely

Where businesses wire AI directly into their systems, Anthropic describes API use as automation-dominant. API workflows often follow more rigid rules than Claude.ai conversations, which reduces the need for human guidance to finish a task. The January 2026 report put Office and Administrative Support at 13% of API transcripts by November 2025, up 3 percentage points — routine back-office work like email handling, document processing, CRM updates and scheduling.

The specific workflows spreading fastest are telling. Two job categories saw their API workflows double between November 2025 and February 2026: business sales and outreach automation — lead research and qualification, customer data updates, email drafting, sales content — and automated trading. Customer service workflows, especially automated support for payment and billing issues, remain a mainstay of the API data. These are task categories whose share of sampled API traffic grew; the report does not measure effects on headcount.

### Coding is still the deep end

Coding tasks continue to migrate from augmentative use on Claude.ai toward more automated workflows in Anthropic's first-party API, and Claude.ai usage itself got less concentrated: the top 10 tasks made up 19% of traffic in February 2026, down from 24% in November 2025. Software-related tasks are still the largest share of sampled Claude.ai conversations. That is a statement about Claude.ai usage, not about all remote work.

### Distribution is what makes this feel sudden

One reason AI can feel more present at work, in my view, is bundling. Zoom announced in September 2023 that AI Companion was included at no additional cost for customers with paid services in their Zoom user accounts ([Zoom announcement](https://news.zoom.com/zoom-ai-companion/)). That's still the policy, with a caveat worth knowing: AI Companion comes at no additional cost with paid Zoom user accounts, but specialized AI Companion products and custom configurations may require additional fees.

When meeting AI becomes a checkbox inside a subscription you already pay for, adoption stops being a decision and becomes a default. That makes "is your team using AI?" a less useful question than "for what, and with what review?" (my view).

Geography shows some convergence within the US. From August 2025 to February 2026, the share of per-person Claude usage going to the top five US states fell from 30% to 24%, as reported at the time of writing. Anthropic says US convergence continued but at a slower pace, and that across countries usage became slightly more concentrated.

## Three Layers, Not One Number

![anthropic.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/how-much-of-remote-work-is-actually-run-by-ai-now/3.png)
*Screenshot of anthropic.com ([source](https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-index-primitives))*

"How much of remote work is run by AI" is the wrong unit of measurement, and that's why every answer you've read feels either wildly overstated or uselessly cautious. Here's how I'd carve it up instead.

1. **The documentation layer** — notes, summaries, recaps, status updates, meeting minutes, first-pass drafts, ticket descriptions. In my view, AI is used heavily here; the studies cited above don't measure how much of this material humans edit.
2. **The production layer** — code, decks, analyses, outreach sequences, support replies. AI drafts, a human approves. This is the contested middle, and it's where the augmentation-versus-automation numbers keep sloshing back and forth.
3. **The judgment layer** — what to build, who to hire, which client to fire, whether a number is wrong. I'd expect humans to keep ownership of most of these decisions, but that is my judgment, not a measured figure.

**My concern with headline percentages:** averaging these three layers into one number hides more than it shows. "AI does 30% of work" would, in my opinion, understate layer one and overstate layer three.

A second opinion: automation isn't necessarily the scary endpoint, and augmentation isn't necessarily the safe one. The automated work Anthropic describes — billing support, document processing, lead enrichment — is routine. Layer two is what I'd watch, because drafts good enough to approve quickly can let review quality slip. The studies cited here don't measure that.

**To the skeptical reader who says this is overblown:** look at the API data, not the chat data. Chat usage is visible and feels incremental. API usage sits inside products and internal tooling where users never see it, and that's where the doubling workflows showed up.

**To the reader who says AI already runs everything:** one reading of the March 2026 release counts measurable Claude usage in only 7.5% of the roughly 18,000 O*NET task statements. None of the cited studies measures how much of remote work as a whole runs end to end on AI.

## The Strongest Counterargument

![news.zoom.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/how-much-of-remote-work-is-actually-run-by-ai-now/4.png)
*Screenshot of news.zoom.com ([source](https://news.zoom.com/zoom-ai-companion/))*

The fairest objection to my position is that usage telemetry from one AI vendor is not the economy. Anthropic is careful about this: Claude is used for high-value, complex work that isn't broadly representative of the US economy, and adoption is uneven — more intense in high-income countries and in US places with more knowledge workers. Claude users are not a random sample of workers.

There's also a drift in who's using it. The March 2026 report found Claude adoption broadening to lower-wage tasks as use cases diversified, which cuts against the "it's just programmers" caricature but also means the sample keeps changing underneath the trend lines.

So yes: my view of the documentation layer probably fits knowledge-work-heavy, laptop-first companies best, and fits a remote claims processor at a regional insurer less well.

## Bottom Line

**Who should care:** anyone whose remote job is mostly producing documents about work rather than doing the work.

**What to actually do:**

- **Audit your week by layer, not by tool.** If more than half your hours land in layer one, in my view that's an exposure, not a productivity win waiting to happen.
- **Stop paying for AI you already own.** Bundled AI in conferencing and office suites overlaps with standalone note-takers. Check what's included before you renew a second subscription.
- **Move up a layer deliberately.** The durable skill is being able to tell when confident-sounding output is wrong.
- **If you manage people:** protect the junior pipeline. Routine tasks that AI handles well are often the tasks people used to learn judgment on (my opinion).

## FAQ

**Is AI replacing remote jobs or just remote tasks?**
These data describe tasks, not employment. Anthropic's usage reports track what Claude is used for and cannot show whether jobs are being replaced.

**Which remote work is most AI-run right now?**
In Anthropic's samples, software-related tasks are the largest share of Claude.ai conversations, and the January 2026 report put Office and Administrative Support at 13% of API transcripts by November 2025. These samples do not cover all remote work.

**Do I need to pay for AI meeting tools?**
Probably not as a separate line item. Zoom includes AI Companion at no additional cost with paid Zoom user accounts, though specialized AI Companion products and custom configurations can cost extra. Buy a dedicated tool only if you have a real gap the bundled version can't cover.

**Will AI usage keep spreading outside tech hubs?**
Within the US, per-person Claude usage has been converging, though more slowly than before — the top five states' share fell from 30% to 24% between August 2025 and February 2026. Anthropic notes that across countries, usage became slightly more concentrated.

*Updated October 2026: this post is based on Anthropic's published Economic Index reports and Zoom's own announcement, not on any test I ran; figures I could not confirm in the source reports have been removed or marked as reported at the time of writing.*

## My Take

My read is that the interesting number isn't the augmentation/automation split at all. It flipped three times in four samples — automation led 49% to 47% in August, then augmentation led 52% to 45%, then augmentation ticked up again in March. A metric that noisy can't carry the weight people put on it. Watch the API side instead, where the direction has been consistent.

I think the practical risk for most remote workers isn't being replaced; it's getting stuck producing layer-one artifacts that an API call already generates for someone else's company. If your calendar is mostly recaps and status docs, that's a signal, and I'd act on it this quarter rather than next year.

The fair point on the other side: all of this is one vendor's telemetry, and measurable Claude usage still shows up in a small minority of catalogued work tasks. The economy-wide picture could be far less dramatic than the Claude-user picture.

I'm not an economist or a financial adviser, and nothing here is career or investment advice. But if I had to bet on one habit, it's building the ability to spot wrong-but-confident output — that's the part the data keeps showing machines doing least well on their own.
